wiping-after-using-the-bathroom.d: Wiping front to back until the paper comes back clean.
wiping-after-using-the-bathroom.h: Take your time, use moist wipes if needed, and check paper until clean.

washing-private-areas.d: Using gentle soap and warm water to wash private parts in the shower or bath.
washing-private-areas.h: Use warm water, mild soap, and gently wash private parts cleanly.

brushing-my-teeth.d: Brushing all teeth with toothpaste twice every day.
brushing-my-teeth.h: Brush in tiny circles for 2 minutes—top, bottom, front, and back!

flossing-my-teeth.d: Using string or a floss stick to clean between my teeth.
flossing-my-teeth.h: Use a colorful floss pick and gently slide between teeth once a day.

brushing-my-tongue.d: Gently brushing my tongue so my mouth feels fresh.
brushing-my-tongue.h: Stick out your tongue and sweep softly from back to front 3 times.

cleaning-out-my-ears.d: Washing inside and behind both ears softly with water.
cleaning-out-my-ears.h: Use a warm wet washcloth over your finger to wipe around the ear.

cleaning-skin-folds.d: Washing and drying under skin folds every day.
cleaning-skin-folds.h: Wash gently with soap and pat completely dry with a soft towel.

cleaning-my-belly-button.d: Washing inside belly button with water and soap.
cleaning-my-belly-button.h: Gently wipe inside with soap on your finger during bath time.

cleaning-between-my-toes.d: Getting soap and water between every toe when washing.
cleaning-between-my-toes.h: Wiggle your toes in soapy water and dry between them after.

cleaning-my-neck-and-chin.d: Washing around the front, back of my neck, and under my chin.
cleaning-my-neck-and-chin.h: Tilt chin up and wipe in gentle circles with warm soapy water.

how-much-deodorant-to-use.d: Putting the right amount of deodorant stick under my arms every morning.
how-much-deodorant-to-use.h: Swipe up and down 2 or 3 times under each arm after dressing.

cutting-my-fingernails.d: Trimming fingernails safely so they do not hurt or get dirty.
cutting-my-fingernails.h: Ask a helper to clip fingernails after bath time when nails are soft.

cutting-my-toenails.d: Trimming toenails straight across so they grow nicely.
cutting-my-toenails.h: Cut straight across so the corners don't poke your skin.

washing-my-hair-with-shampoo.d: Putting shampoo in wet hair, rubbing my head, and rinsing it all out.
washing-my-hair-with-shampoo.h: Close eyes tightly, massage shampoo like making bubbles, then rinse well.

using-hair-conditioner.d: Putting conditioner on hair ends so it brushes smoothly.
using-hair-conditioner.h: Put a penny-size drop on hair ends, count to 10, then rinse with water.

brushing-my-hair.d: Gently combing hair so it does not have tangles.
brushing-my-hair.h: Start brushing at the bottom ends of hair first, then work up to the top.

washing-my-hands-after-bathroom.d: Using soap and warm water for 20 seconds after using the toilet.
washing-my-hands-after-bathroom.h: Sing 'Happy Birthday' twice while scrubbing hands with soap and water.

washing-hands-before-eating.d: Washing hands with soap before touching food.
washing-hands-before-eating.h: Scrub palms, backs of hands, and fingers before sitting down to eat.

blowing-my-nose-into-a-tissue.d: Blowing nose softly, throwing tissue away, and washing hands.
blowing-my-nose-into-a-tissue.h: Press one side shut, blow out softly, throw away tissue, and wash hands.

taking-care-of-cuts-and-scrapes.d: Washing a small cut, drying it, and putting a band-aid on.
taking-care-of-cuts-and-scrapes.h: Rinse cut under cool water, pat dry, and cover with a cute bandage.

knowing-when-i-have-to-pee-or-poop.d: Going to the bathroom right away before it becomes an emergency or an accident.
knowing-when-i-have-to-pee-or-poop.h: Stop playing right away when tummy feels full pressure and walk to bathroom.

pulling-pants-up-and-down.d: Pulling my pants and underwear all the way down before sitting on the potty, and all the way up after.
pulling-pants-up-and-down.h: Pull garments all the way down to knees before sitting, pull up to waist after.

flushing-the-potty.d: Pushing the toilet handle down every time after I use the bathroom.
flushing-the-potty.h: Push handle down until water swirls, then close toilet lid.

rinsing-all-the-soap-off.d: Using clean water to wash away all soap bubbles from skin and hair so skin does not itch.
rinsing-all-the-soap-off.h: Rinse body with water until skin feels clean and smooth, no slippery soap left.

washing-and-drying-my-face.d: Washing food or dirt off my face with water and drying softly with a towel.
washing-and-drying-my-face.h: Splash cool water on face, wipe gently with soft washcloth, pat dry.

spitting-out-toothpaste.d: Spitting all the toothpaste into the sink when I am done brushing, not swallowing it.
spitting-out-toothpaste.h: Lean over sink, spit out foam, rinse mouth with a tiny sip of water.

changing-hygiene-pads.d: Taking off dirty pads, putting clean ones on underwear, and wrapping dirty ones up.
changing-hygiene-pads.h: Peel off old pad, wrap in toilet paper, throw in trash, stick new pad on.

washing-up-during-periods.d: Keeping private parts clean and dry when bleeding happens.
washing-up-during-periods.h: Use warm water and soft wipes to stay fresh and dry throughout the day.

wearing-a-supportive-bra.d: Putting on a comfortable bra so the chest feels supported.
wearing-a-supportive-bra.h: Choose soft fabrics that feel good and don't pinch or feel too tight.

washing-male-private-parts.d: Washing gently around the penis and testicles with warm water.
washing-male-private-parts.h: Use warm water and mild soap to wash gently around private parts every bath.

changing-athletic-or-supportive-underwea.d: Wearing clean, supportive underwear every day so body feels comfortable.
changing-athletic-or-supportive-underwea.h: Put on fresh, comfortable boxers or briefs every morning after washing.

facial-hair-shaving-safety.d: Knowing how to trim or shave facial hair safely with an adult.
facial-hair-shaving-safety.h: Ask an adult to guide you with shaving cream and safety razor tools.

picking-weather-clothes.d: Wearing warm clothes when cold and light clothes when hot.
picking-weather-clothes.h: Look outside or check the weather: sweater for cold, shorts for sun!

matching-my-clothes.d: Picking tops and bottoms that look nice together.
matching-my-clothes.h: Pick favorite colors that match or ask a helper to help pick an outfit.

changing-clean-underwear-every-day.d: Putting on fresh, clean underwear every single morning.
changing-clean-underwear-every-day.h: Put clean underwear on right after morning wash or getting dressed.

left-and-right-shoes.d: Putting shoes on the correct feet every time.
left-and-right-shoes.h: Put shoes together so the inside curves look like they are hugging.

tying-shoe-laces.d: Tying laces into a double knot so shoes stay on.
tying-shoe-laces.h: Make bunny ears with the laces, cross them over, pull loop through!

buttons-and-zippers.d: Buttoning shirts and pulling up zippers on pants on my own.
buttons-and-zippers.h: Push button half through hole first, then pull from the other side.

clean-vs-dirty-clothes.d: Knowing when clothes are dirty and putting them in the laundry box.
clean-vs-dirty-clothes.h: If it has food, smells, or was worn all day, toss it into the hamper.

folding-clean-clothes.d: Folding shirts and pants gently to put away in drawers.
folding-clean-clothes.h: Lay shirt flat, fold sleeves in, fold in half, put neatly in drawer.

morning-and-bedtime-routines.d: Following a simple morning routine and bedtime step list.
morning-and-bedtime-routines.h: Check a picture chart for what steps come next in morning and night.

cleaning-up-my-mess.d: Putting trash in the bin and picking up items off the floor.
cleaning-up-my-mess.h: Pick up 5 items at a time and put them in their home spots.

wiping-tables-after-eating.d: Using a damp cloth to wipe crumbs off the table.
wiping-tables-after-eating.h: Wipe from back of table to front into your hand or a napkin.

making-my-bed.d: Pulling sheets and blankets up neatly on my bed.
making-my-bed.h: Pull pillow to head of bed, pull blanket all the way up to pillow.

checking-locked-doors-at-night.d: Making sure house doors are closed and locked safely.
checking-locked-doors-at-night.h: Walk to front and back doors with a helper to check locks before sleep.

drinking-enough-water.d: Drinking cups of fresh water throughout the day.
drinking-enough-water.h: Keep a water bottle nearby and take 3 big gulps every hour.

knowing-when-i-am-hungry-or-full.d: Listening to my stomach when it needs food and stopping when full.
knowing-when-i-am-hungry-or-full.h: Check in with your tummy before, during, and after eating meals.

using-forks-and-spoons.d: Holding utensils properly to eat food safely.
using-forks-and-spoons.h: Hold spoon or fork handle like a pencil to scoop up bites easily.

using-a-butter-knife.d: Cutting soft food slowly without hurting my fingers.
using-a-butter-knife.h: Keep fingers away from blade, press down gently on soft food.

hot-stove-safety.d: Knowing the stove, oven, and hot water can burn skin.
hot-stove-safety.h: Stay 3 big steps back from hot stoves, ovens, and hot pans.

making-a-simple-snack.d: Getting a clean snack like fruit, bread, or cheese by myself.
making-a-simple-snack.h: Pick an easy snack like an apple, banana, or cheese stick from fridge.

making-toast-or-a-sandwich.d: Using the toaster or spreading butter/peanut butter safely.
making-toast-or-a-sandwich.h: Spread butter softly across bread, ask an adult to help push toaster.

keeping-food-in-the-fridge.d: Putting cold items like milk or yogurt back in the fridge right away.
keeping-food-in-the-fridge.h: Put milk and yogurt back in fridge as soon as you finish pouring.

knowing-what-is-safe-to-eat.d: Knowing to only put food in my mouth and never eating toys, trash, or things off the floor.
knowing-what-is-safe-to-eat.h: Only put real food from kitchen or plate into mouth. Ask if unsure.

chewing-with-mouth-closed.d: Taking small bites and chewing food with my lips together so food stays inside.
chewing-with-mouth-closed.h: Take small bites, close lips together, chew 10 times before swallowing.

drinking-without-spilling.d: Holding a cup with two hands and drinking slowly so liquids do not spill on clothes.
drinking-without-spilling.h: Hold cup with both hands, tilt slowly, swallow before taking another sip.

knowing-if-food-smells-bad-or-spoiled.d: Asking an adult before eating food that smells weird, looks bad, or has mold.
knowing-if-food-smells-bad-or-spoiled.h: If food smells sour, looks funny, or has spots, show an adult first.

wiping-mouth-after-eating.d: Using a napkin to wipe food off my mouth and hands after I finish eating.
wiping-mouth-after-eating.h: Use napkin to wipe corners of mouth and fingers clean right after eating.

private-parts-privacy.d: Knowing my private parts belong only to me and keeping them covered.
private-parts-privacy.h: Keep private areas covered with clothes and keep bathroom doors closed.

closing-the-bathroom-door.d: Shutting the door when using the toilet or showering for privacy.
closing-the-bathroom-door.h: Close the door all the way before taking off clothes or sitting on potty.

safe-touch-and-boundaries.d: Saying 'No' or asking for help if anyone makes me uncomfortable.
safe-touch-and-boundaries.h: Say loudly 'Stop, I don't like that!' and go tell a safe helper right away.

personal-space.d: Not standing too close to people unless I ask first.
personal-space.h: Keep one arm length of distance between you and other people.

knowing-who-to-call-in-emergency.d: Knowing when to get a trusted person or call for help if hurt or scared.
knowing-who-to-call-in-emergency.h: Know how to dial 911 or call your safe helper's phone number.

looking-both-ways-on-streets.d: Looking left, right, and left again before walking across roads.
looking-both-ways-on-streets.h: Hold an adult's hand, stop at the curb, look left, right, and left again.

leaving-cuts-and-scabs-alone.d: Not picking at cuts or scabs so skin can heal safely.
leaving-cuts-and-scabs-alone.h: If scab itches, put a band-aid over it or pat gently instead of scratching.

taking-medicine-only-with-adult-help.d: Never touching or taking pills or medicine unless given directly by an adult.
taking-medicine-only-with-adult-help.h: Never touch bottles or pills. Only take medicine given by a safe helper.

telling-where-my-body-hurts.d: Using words to point and say when my tummy, head, or skin hurts.
telling-where-my-body-hurts.h: Point to where it hurts and say: 'My [head/tummy/arm] hurts right here'.

telling-when-i-feel-sick-or-dizzy.d: Telling an adult right away when I feel weak, hot, dizzy, or thrown up.
telling-when-i-feel-sick-or-dizzy.h: Sit down on floor right away and call out to helper: 'I feel sick/dizzy!'

never-opening-doors-to-strangers.d: Asking an adult before opening the front door when someone knocks.
never-opening-doors-to-strangers.h: When door knocks, freeze! Call an adult to open the door.

staying-away-from-cleaning-liquids.d: Never touching spray bottles, bleach, or cleaning liquids.
staying-away-from-cleaning-liquids.h: Leave spray bottles, soap pods, and cleaning liquids alone.

not-hitting-or-biting-when-mad.d: Keeping hands and body safe when angry instead of throwing things or hitting.
not-hitting-or-biting-when-mad.h: Squeeze a pillow, stomp feet twice, or hug yourself tightly instead of hitting.

being-gentle-with-pets-and-animals.d: Petting dogs and cats softly, never squeezing, hitting, or pulling tails.
being-gentle-with-pets-and-animals.h: Use soft hand flat against fur, pet softly from head to back.

hurting-people-or-pets-is-wrong.d: Knowing it is bad to hit, kick, push, or hurt anyone or any animal.
hurting-people-or-pets-is-wrong.h: Keep hands gentle, use words when mad instead of physical actions.

asking-before-taking-things.d: Not taking things that belong to others without asking first.
asking-before-taking-things.h: Ask clearly: 'May I play with this please?' before touching someone's things.

naming-my-feelings.d: Using words when I feel mad, sad, scared, tired, or happy.
naming-my-feelings.h: Use emotion cards or say out loud: 'I feel [mad / sad / scared] right now'.

breathing-to-calm-down.d: Taking big deep breaths when my body feels tight or upset.
breathing-to-calm-down.h: Smell the flower (breathe in through nose), blow out the candle (out through mouth).

asking-for-a-quiet-break.d: Telling someone I need quiet time before I get too mad or scared.
asking-for-a-quiet-break.h: Say: 'I need a 5 minute quiet break please' and step into a calm room.

feeling-safe-with-trusted-people.d: Telling trusted helpers the truth when I am scared, hurt, or made a mistake.
feeling-safe-with-trusted-people.h: Remember safe helpers love you and want to help you solve problems.

knowing-mistakes-are-okay.d: Knowing nobody is perfect and it is okay to try again.
knowing-mistakes-are-okay.h: Say: 'Mistakes help me learn. I can fix it or try again next time.'

knowing-when-my-body-is-tired.d: Recognizing when I need to rest or go to sleep.
knowing-when-my-body-is-tired.h: When eyes feel heavy or yawning happens, put screens away and lay down.

worried-thoughts-in-my-mind-anxiety.d: Feeling like thoughts are spinning or bad things might happen.
worried-thoughts-in-my-mind-anxiety.h: Name 3 blue things you see in the room, take 3 slow belly breaths, or squeeze a fidget.

scared-or-shaky-body-feelings-anxiety.d: Fast heart beat, shaky hands, or butterfly feelings in tummy.
scared-or-shaky-body-feelings-anxiety.h: Put one hand on heart and one on tummy, blow out candle breaths, or wrap in a weighted blanket.

feeling-extra-sad-or-heavy-depression.d: Feeling empty, super sad, or like nothing feels fun today.
feeling-extra-sad-or-heavy-depression.h: Wrap up in a warm blanket, hug a stuffed animal, tell a helper 'I feel heavy today'.

getting-stuck-in-bed-or-chair-depression.d: Hard to move body or start doing things when feeling low.
getting-stuck-in-bed-or-chair-depression.h: Try a tiny step: wiggle your toes, sit up, or drink 1 sip of water.

triggers-and-scary-memories-ptsd.d: A sound, smell, or sight suddenly makes me feel scared or remembered bad times.
triggers-and-scary-memories-ptsd.h: Remind yourself: 'I am safe right now in this room.' Touch 3 solid things around you.

flashbacks-ptsd.d: Feeling like a scary past event is happening right now.
flashbacks-ptsd.h: Look at your feet on the floor. Rub your sensory cube. Say out loud: 'Today is [day], I am safe'.

feeling-jumpy-or-watching-for-danger-pts.d: Feeling constantly on guard or easily startled by small sounds.
feeling-jumpy-or-watching-for-danger-pts.h: Sit with your back against a sturdy wall, hold a pillow tightly, take deep breaths.

feeling-safe-inside-my-body-ptsd.d: Feeling disconnected from my body or like I floated away.
feeling-safe-inside-my-body-ptsd.h: Press feet hard into the floor, squeeze your hands into fists and release, sip cold water.

monsters-and-scary-movie-things-are-pret.d: Knowing monsters, ghosts, and scary movie creatures are pretend and cannot touch or hurt me.
monsters-and-scary-movie-things-are-pret.h: Remind yourself: 'That is just costume, makeup, or cartoon drawings'.

shadows-and-night-noises-cannot-hurt-me.d: Knowing shadows on the wall and house noises at night are just shadows and house sounds.
shadows-and-night-noises-cannot-hurt-me.h: Turn on nightlight, look at shadow shape, remember house makes creak sounds when settling.

tv-and-cartoons-are-make-believe.d: Knowing things on screens or TV are pretend stories made by people.
tv-and-cartoons-are-make-believe.h: Remember actors are playing pretend just like playing with toys.

bad-dreams-are-just-thoughts-in-my-head.d: Knowing nightmares are not real life and I am safe when I wake up.
bad-dreams-are-just-thoughts-in-my-head.h: Wake up, look around bedroom, hug blanket, say: 'Dream is gone, I am safe'.

true-words-vs-pretend-words.d: Knowing the difference between telling true words (what really happened) and making up stories.
true-words-vs-pretend-words.h: Tell what really happened first, then say if you want to make up a fun game.

saying-sorry-when-i-make-a-mistake.d: Saying 'I am sorry' if I bump someone, break something, or make someone sad.
saying-sorry-when-i-make-a-mistake.h: Look at person, say softly: 'I am sorry I bumped you. Are you okay?'

asking-for-help.d: Saying 'Can you help me please?' when a job feels too hard.
asking-for-help.h: Take a deep breath and ask: 'Can you help me with this please?'

taking-turns-in-conversation.d: Talking and then stopping so the other person can have a turn.
taking-turns-in-conversation.h: Say your thought, then pause and ask: 'What do you think?'

knowing-when-someone-needs-space.d: Noticing if someone wants quiet time or step-back distance.
knowing-when-someone-needs-space.h: If someone looks away or steps back, give them two big steps of space.

using-inside-voice-volume.d: Matching how loud I talk to where I am (quiet inside, louder outside).
using-inside-voice-volume.h: Use whispering or quiet voice inside rooms, save big yelling voices for outdoors.

using-a-gentle-voice-tone.d: Noticing if my voice sounds angry, sharp, or flat when talking.
using-a-gentle-voice-tone.h: Take a breath before speaking, use soft words, and add a friendly smile.

knowing-when-to-pause-a-habit.d: Stopping picking, watching screens, or doing things too much.
knowing-when-to-pause-a-habit.h: Set a timer on a phone or clock, move to another room when timer rings.

asking-for-help-with-strong-urges.d: Telling a trusted person when I feel a strong push to do a bad habit.
asking-for-help-with-strong-urges.h: Tell a safe helper: 'My body has a strong urge, can you help me find something else to do?'
